name: DCShadow - Rogue Domain Controller Persistence
description: DCShadow registers a rogue domain controller in AD and pushes malicious replication changes (like adding a user to Domain Admins) through normal DC-to-DC replication. Changes made via DCShadow bypass most SIEM detections because they appear as legitimate replication events. Requires DA-level access - this is a persistence technique, not initial access.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
DCShadow temporarily registers the attacker machine as a DC in AD.
It then pushes changes via normal DRS replication protocol.
After the change replicates, the rogue DC is deregistered.

=== REQUIRES ===
- Domain Admin or Enterprise Admin privileges
- Two mimikatz instances running simultaneously

=== STEP 1: SET UP CHANGES (Terminal 1 - SYSTEM) ===
  mimikatz# lsadump::dcshadow /object:TargetUser /attribute:primaryGroupID /value:512
  # 512 = Domain Admins

=== STEP 2: PUSH REPLICATION (Terminal 2 - DA) ===
  mimikatz# lsadump::dcshadow /push
  # This triggers replication from the rogue DC

=== WHAT YOU CAN CHANGE ===
- Add user to Domain Admins (primaryGroupID=512)
- Modify SIDHistory for cross-domain persistence
- Set SPN for Kerberoasting targets
- Modify ACLs for persistent access
- Push any LDAP attribute change

=== WHY ITS STEALTHY ===
Changes come through DRS replication, which is:
- Expected traffic between DCs
- Not logged by standard security events
- Appears as normal AD replication
Only the temporary SPN registration is detectable.

examples.label: Add user to Domain Admins via DCShadow

recommended.note: AdminSDHolder is another stealthy persistence technique.

defense.why_it_works: AD replication (DRS) is a trusted mechanism between DCs. By temporarily registering as a DC, changes are pushed through the same channel legitimate DCs use, bypassing most change-detection systems that monitor LDAP modifications.
defense.prerequisites: Domain Admin privileges; ability to run two mimikatz processes simultaneously.
defense.impact: Stealthy persistent access; any AD attribute can be modified without generating standard change events.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1207] New DC SPN registration (temporary); replication from non-DC IP addresses; Event 4742 showing computer account SPN changes.
defense.artifacts: Temporary SPN registration (GC/ and E3514235-...) on a non-DC computer; Directory Service replication metadata from unknown source.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4742
| where ServicePrincipalNames="*GC/*" OR ServicePrincipalNames="*E3514235-*"
| where NOT match(TargetUserName, "DC\d+\$")
| table _time, TargetUserName, ServicePrincipalNames, SubjectUserName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4742
| where ServicePrincipalNames has "GC/" or ServicePrincipalNames has "E3514235-"
| where TargetUserName !startswith "DC"
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, ServicePrincipalNames, SubjectUserName
defense.prevention: Monitor for DC SPN registration on non-DC computers; use AD replication metadata monitoring; restrict Domain Admin usage; implement Privileged Access Workstations.

detections.name: DCShadow - Rogue DC SPN registration
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4742
| where ServicePrincipalNames has "GC/" or ServicePrincipalNames has "E3514235-4B06-11D1-AB04-00C04FC2DCD2"
| join kind=anti (
    SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4742 | where TargetUserName in ("DC01$", "DC02$")
) on TargetUserName
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, ServicePrincipalNames, SubjectUserName
detections.false_positives: Legitimate DC promotion; DVDC (domain controller VMs being promoted)
detections.tuning: Whitelist known DC computer accounts; alert on any non-DC getting replication SPNs
